clue.text: After science, raw beginner will write hurriedly

parts.note: SC is a standard abbreviation for science
taken as written
L, the learner plate, stands for a beginner

explanation.surface: A novice in science is going to rush out some notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just sets the order: SC comes first, then RAW, then L.
explanation.definitionFit: To scribble something quickly and untidily is a synonym for writing in haste.

clue.text: Plant a short time in the vehicle coming up

indicators.note: the shortened hour sits inside the turned vehicle word
in a down clue, coming up means the vehicle word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
HR is the short form of hour, a short time

explanation.surface: Someone loads a plant into a van for a brief trip uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns BUS into SUB, and HR goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bush is a woody plant smaller than a tree, an example of plant life.

clue.text: Point of attack

parts.note: read literally, the pointed tip of a weapon used to strike, the business end of a shaft fired from a bow

explanation.surface: A military phrase for where an assault begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The sharp tip of a missile fired from a bow is literally the point that does the attacking.

clue.text: Tactile manipulation of framework

indicators.note: manipulating something works it about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Handling a structure by touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A criss-cross grid of strips, as in a trellis, is a kind of open framework.

clue.text: One gets behind the baseball batsman

definitions.text: One gets behind the baseball batsman

parts.words: One gets behind the baseball batsman
parts.note: describes the fielder (or the fence) placed behind the hitter in baseball

explanation.surface: Describes a position on a baseball field.
explanation.walkthrough: In baseball the catcher crouches behind the batter; the word also names the fence behind home plate.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the catcher who crouches behind home plate is called this, as is the screen there.

clue.text: Made a dramatic introduction

parts.note: means introduced or set in motion, with a nod to putting something on the stage in a drama

explanation.surface: Someone made a theatrical entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning introduced or brought into use, with drama hinting at a stage play.

clue.text: Crawl out of bed and approach silently

definitions.meaning: to crawl is to creep, and out of bed is up, read as creep plus up
to sneak up on someone stealthily

explanation.surface: Someone slips out of bed and sneaks towards another.
explanation.definitionFit: Crawling plus rising from bed gives the phrase, which as an idiom means to sneak towards someone unseen.

clue.text: Four in test of little value

indicators.note: the Roman numeral for four is placed inside the word for test

parts.note: a trial is a test
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four in a cricket Test match counts for little.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a boundary in a cricket Test (a four), but Four is the Roman numeral IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unimportant or insignificant is of little worth.

clue.text: Penny mentioned that it was more popular

parts.note: to refer to something is to mention it

explanation.surface: Penny remarked that something was more in demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned' looks like a sound signal but simply means REFERRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chosen ahead of others is favoured, that is, liked better.

clue.text: Feel sorry for unfortunate Gert about to be included

indicators.note: the word for about is to be put inside the scrambled name
something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters of the name are jumbled

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone pities poor Gert, who is about to be let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunate' turns GERT into REGT, and 'to be included' puts RE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to wish it had not happened, a synonym of feeling sorry.

clue.text: Too particular, finding nothing right in an Italian city

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the city name

parts.note: Venice is a city in Italy

explanation.surface: A fussy person finds nothing correct in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside VENICE to give VERNICE, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessively fastidious or fussy describes someone overly particular.

clue.text: Poet confessing to opening lines

indicators.note: the railway lines open the word, so they are placed at the front

parts.note: BR, British Rail, ran Britain's railway lines
owning (up) means admitting or confessing

explanation.surface: A poet admits to the first lines of a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening lines' looks like a poem's first verse; but British Rail ran the railway lines, and 'opening' says that abbreviation comes at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning and Elizabeth Barrett Browning were Victorian poets.

clue.text: Swimmer I found in a particular spot

indicators.note: the I is located inside the word for a spot

parts.note: a place is a particular spot

explanation.surface: A swimmer says they turned up in a certain location.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish is a sea creature, and crosswords often call fish swimmers.

clue.text: 'as to put mortar round the window

indicators.note: the mortar word is placed around the other letters

parts.note: cement is a mortar for binding bricks
the dropped-aitch has, written as is, read as its letters

explanation.surface: A Cockney builder says he has to put mortar round the window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as is a Cockney 'has' (dropping the h), giving AS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged window that opens like a door is a specific kind of window.

clue.text: Cows reported on Iona moved to part of Spain

indicators.note: reported means said aloud, so the herd word is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: cows are cattle

indicators.note: the letters of the island name are moved about

explanation.surface: Word comes that cows on a Scottish island were shipped to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a small Scottish island; 'moved' rearranges it to ONIA after CATAL, the sound of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A region in north-east Spain with Barcelona as its capital, an example of a part of Spain.

clue.text: Tree found on the Isle of Dogs

definitions.text: found on the Isle of Dogs
definitions.meaning: a district of East London that includes the Isle of Dogs peninsula

explanation.surface: A tree growing on a peninsula in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Dogs is a peninsula in East London's Docklands; the district of the same name as the tree takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: A common tree, and also the East London district covering the Docklands peninsula.

clue.text: Officer will reimburse teacher

parts.note: to pay someone back is to reimburse them
a schoolmaster is a teacher

explanation.surface: An officer promises to repay a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: An official, often military, responsible for paying wages is an officer.

clue.text: Merchant ship

definitions.meaning: a dealer who buys and sells

explanation.surface: A merchant vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a dealer in goods and a vessel carrying cargo for commerce.

clue.text: We were overdrawn a couple of newcomers first acknowledged

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'We were overdrawn a couple of newcomers first acknowledged' (7): ALLOWED = acknowledged, and A + LL (two learners) + OWED fits, but 'We were overdrawn' cannot give OWED cleanly and the clue seems garbled; no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: We were overdrawn a couple of newcomers first acknowledged

clue.text: Most embarrassed?

parts.note: the most embarrassed person is the one whose face has flushed the deepest colour

explanation.surface: Asks who felt the most shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Blushing is a sign of embarrassment, so the most embarrassed face has the strongest flush.

clue.text: One who has recently joined the union

definitions.text: One who has recently joined the union

parts.words: One who has recently joined the union
parts.note: union read as marriage rather than a trade union: a person just married

explanation.surface: Describes a new trade union member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union but means marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A person just married has recently entered the union of matrimony.

clue.text: Unsettled weather-wind

indicators.note: unsettled describes something disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Changeable weather and gusty wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' rhymes with blind here: to twist or entwine.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist or coil around something, as with a garland, is to wind.

clue.text: Girl and boy sung merrily

parts.note: Lil is a girl's name
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl and a boy sang cheerfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing with a lively rhythmic lilt is to sing cheerfully.

clue.text: Telephonist in the theatre?

definitions.meaning: a person who connects calls at a switchboard
a surgeon working in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: A switchboard worker at a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests a playhouse but means an operating theatre, where the surgeon works.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a switchboard worker and a surgeon who performs operations.

clue.text: Railway goes round ebbing river covered with grass

indicators.note: the railway letters surround the turned river name
ebbing means flowing back, so the river name is read backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: A railway line skirts a falling river overgrown with grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ebbing' turns DEE into EED, and 'goes round' puts RY around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of reeds, tall grasses growing by water, means grassy in that sense.

clue.text: Filmed report coming from all quarters on a cylinder

parts.note: N, E, W and S are the four compass points, all the quarters
a reel is a cylinder on which film is wound

explanation.surface: Footage gathered from everywhere stored on a spool.
explanation.definitionFit: A short cinema film of current events is a filmed bulletin.

clue.text: The story about an abstainer is just gossip

indicators.note: the story word goes around the abstainer letters

parts.note: a tale is a story
TT, teetotal, describes an abstainer from alcohol

explanation.surface: The tale told about a teetotaller is mere hearsay.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle chatter about others is a synonym for gossip.

clue.text: Entry lad vandalised in a fiery way

indicators.note: vandalised means smashed up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy breaks in and wrecks the place in a passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionately or with burning zeal is the manner of acting fierily.

clue.text: Hearty concoction that is gross

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture made up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A hearty mixture that is coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude or coarse humour is described as gross.
